HOW TO USE

Type a short story and press Run once: a local AI splits it into 6 scenes and writes a picture prompt for each, Klein draws all 6 in the same style, and Image Grid lays them out as a storyboard. The scenes are also saved one by one.

 Steps

  1. Type your story in the box of AI Prompt Pixaroma: a few sentences are enough.
  2. Pick a style in Text Join Two Pixaroma (the second box), for example comic book, bold lines or cinematic film still.
  3. Press Run.

 Good to know

  • Want 4 or 9 scenes? Change the number in the formula (the gear of AI Prompt) AND the columns of Image Grid.
  • The AI's seed is Fixed, so the same story gives the same scenes. Set it to R for new ones.
  • Fewer pictures than scenes? The small AI sometimes writes fewer lines (with this story, 3 of 6 AI seeds wrote all 6; the workflow uses one that does). Change the AI's seed and Run again.
  • The same character in every picture is the hard part: the formula makes the AI describe her the same way each time, and a fixed Klein seed helps. For a perfect match, edit one picture into the others with an edit workflow.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

What AI Prompt needs Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Flux 2 Klein 9B) - The image model, Flux 2 Klein 9B from Black Forest Labs. It is a fast 4-step model that can make a picture from words AND change a picture you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen 3 8B, reads the prompt) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the image model understands.
  • Load VAE (Flux 2) - Turns the finished render into a picture you can see, and a picture into the model's own format.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3.5 4B, writes the scenes) - The language model that WRITES the scene prompts, Qwen3.5 4B. Klein's own text encoder can only read, it cannot write, so the writer is a separate, small model.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • AI Prompt Pixaroma (1. your story, split into 6 scenes) - Your story goes in its box. Its formula (the gear) asks for exactly 6 scene prompts, one per line, with the main character described the same way every time, so all the pictures show the same character.
  • Text Join Two Pixaroma (2. one style for every scene) - Adds the SAME style to every scene, so the storyboard looks like one book. Change the second box to change the style of all 6.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (3. picture size) - The picture size. Click a size; the Portrait / Landscape switch turns it on its side.
  • Seed Pixaroma (4. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves and do the small jobs: count, pick, join or pass things along.

  • Prompt Each Pixaroma (each line = one scene) - Gets the 6 lines on its text input and sends them through one after the other: one Run, one picture per scene. Its own rows are empty on purpose.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • CLIP Text Encode (reads the prompt) - Reads the prompt through the text encoder.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. Klein runs at CFG 1, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • Empty Flux 2 Latent (blank canvas) - The blank canvas the picture is painted on, at the size it receives.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings Klein is made for.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (each scene, numbered) - Saves every scene as PNG into ComfyUI/output/Storyboard, numbered in order.
  • Image Grid Pixaroma (the storyboard) - Lays the 6 scenes out as a storyboard, 3 per row, numbered 1 to 6, with a title.
  • Save Image Pixaroma (the storyboard sheet) - Saves the storyboard sheet as a JPG into the same folder.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the number of pictures and their size.

WhatTime
The AI writing 6 scenesabout 5 s
Klein drawing 6 picturesabout 12 s
Story to storyboardabout 20 s

Klein needs 4 steps, so it is fast: about 1.7 s for a 1024 x 1024 picture from a prompt and about 3 s for an edit at 1 megapixel, where it also reads your picture.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models from disk (about 18 GB for Klein and its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a 16 GB card

Timed on an RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB with 32 GB of RAM:

  • Klein took about 3 to 6 times as long, about 10 s even for one picture: Klein and its text encoder (17 GB together) do not fit in 16 GB, so parts of them load again on every Run, and a second Run is no faster.
  • The AI text step took about 2 times as long.
